Feluda.description: A private detective and the main protagonist known for his sharp observation and analytical skills.

Tapesh.description: Feluda's cousin and the narrator of the story who accompanies Feluda on his adventures and assists in the investigation.

Baba.description: Tapesh's father, who is unable to join the trip due to a work tour in Bangalore.

Sasadhar Bose.description: A cheerful and talkative man working for a chemical firm who joins Feluda and Tapesh on their journey to Gangtok.

Takla Makan.description: A large desert in northwest China, referenced as a subject Feluda was reading about.

Bagdogra.description: A town in West Bengal, India, with an airport serving as the entry point to the eastern Himalayas.

Gangtok.description: The capital city of Sikkim, a northeastern Indian state in the Himalayas.

Sikkim.description: A small Indian state in the eastern Himalayas, known for its Tibetan cultural influence.

Darjeeling.description: A hill station in West Bengal, India, famous for its tea gardens and scenic beauty.

Bangalore.description: A major city in southern India, now known as Bengaluru.

Calcutta.description: The former name of Kolkata, the capital city of West Bengal, India.

Tibet.description: A region north of Sikkim, now an autonomous region of China.

Sven Hedin.description: A Swedish geographer and explorer, known for his travels in Central Asia and Tibet.

Tibetan.description: Tibetan refers to people from Tibet or their culture; Tibetans are the people of Tibet, many of whom live in Sikkim and are associated with Buddhist culture.

Lachen.description: A town in North Sikkim, known for its scenic beauty.

Lachung.description: Another picturesque town in North Sikkim.

Nathula.description: Nathula is a mountain pass in the Himalayas connecting Sikkim with Tibet; Nathula Road is the road in Gangtok leading towards this pass on the India-China border.

Bombay.description: The former name of Mumbai, the capital city of Maharashtra, India.

S. S. Chemicals.description: The chemical company where Sasadhar Bose works.

Siliguri.description: A city in West Bengal, India, serving as a gateway to the northeast.

Sewak Road.description: A road leading from Siliguri towards Sikkim.

Rongpo.description: A border town between West Bengal and Sikkim.

West Bengal.description: An eastern Indian state, bordering Sikkim.

Tista.description: A major river in Sikkim and West Bengal.

Tista Bazaar.description: A market area near the Tista river.

Air India.description: India's national airline, referenced through a branded bag.

Snow View Hotel.description: The Snow View Hotel, also called Snow View, is the hotel in Gangtok where Feluda and his companions are staying during their investigation.

Nepal.description: A neighboring country to India, north of Sikkim.

Bhutan.description: A Himalayan kingdom east of Sikkim.

Ma.description: Means 'mother' in Bengali and Hindi; here, it is inscribed on a ring as a sign of devotion.

dak bungalow.description: A colonial-era rest house or guesthouse for travelers, often used by government officials in India.

woollens.description: Warm clothing made of wool, commonly used in India to refer to winter wear.

pullover.description: A knitted sweater or jumper, commonly used in Indian English.

air pocket.description: A term used in aviation for a sudden drop in altitude due to turbulence.

Nishikanto Sarkar.description: A Bengali gentleman from Darjeeling who sold a Tibetan statue to Mr Shelvankar and appears nervous after receiving a mysterious note.

Helmut Ungar.description: A German professional photographer staying at the dak bungalow who was an acquaintance of Mr Shelvankar.

Dr Vaidya.description: A mysterious figure who stayed at the dak bungalow, known for his abilities in palmistry and spiritualism, and who unsettled Mr Shelvankar.

Kanchenjunga.description: A prominent Himalayan mountain visible from Sikkim and Darjeeling, famous for its scenic beauty.

Pemiangchi.description: A location near Gangtok, noted for its ruins, forest, and old British-era buildings.

Kalimpong.description: A hill station in West Bengal, near Darjeeling and Sikkim, mentioned as a destination of Dr Vaidya.

Singik.description: A place near Gangtok, mentioned as the destination of Mr Shelvankar on the day of his accident.

Tibetan Institute.description: A local institution in Gangtok dedicated to Tibetan culture and art.

Art Emporium.description: A shop or gallery in Gangtok where art objects are displayed and sold.

Bata.description: A popular footwear brand in India, known for its retail stores across the country.

Indian.description: Relating to India, its people, or culture.

Chinese.description: Relating to China, its people, or culture.

Nepali.description: Relating to Nepal or its people; here, referring to local laborers.

paan.description: A preparation combining betel leaf with areca nut and sometimes tobacco, chewed as a stimulant and mouth freshener.

gumpha.description: A gumpha (plural: gumphas) is a Buddhist monastery, especially in the Himalayan regions, serving as a center for religious practice and community life.

namaskar.description: A traditional Indian greeting, similar to 'hello,' accompanied by a gesture of folded hands.

Mr Shelvankar.description: The owner of S. S. Chemicals who died in a jeep accident near Gangtok after purchasing a Tibetan statue.

Lama.description: Refers to the chief religious figure at Rumtek, described as number three after the Dalai Lama.

North Sikkim Highway.description: A major road in Sikkim, referenced as the site of the accident.

Dalai Lama.description: The spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism, referenced as having met the Institute's curator.

Rumtek.description: A town near Gangtok, famous for its monastery and the Lama dance.

National and Grindlays Bank.description: A British bank with branches in India, referenced as the issuer of the cheque.

Chogyal.description: The Chogyal, also known as the King of Sikkim, was the monarch who ruled Sikkim before its merger with India in 1975.

tankhas.description: Tibetan Buddhist religious paintings on cloth, often depicting deities or mandalas.

Tantrik.description: Relating to Tantra, a set of esoteric traditions rooted in Hindu and Buddhist philosophy.

jeep.description: A type of rugged vehicle commonly used in hilly regions of India.

Yamantak.description: A fierce deity in Tibetan Buddhism, depicted with multiple heads and arms.

sacred intestine.description: A term used for the hollow space in a statue where a prayer scroll is inserted.

darshan.description: A Sanskrit term meaning an auspicious viewing or audience, especially of a deity or holy person.

Lama dance.description: A traditional Tibetan Buddhist ritual dance performed by monks, often during festivals.

Chungtham.description: A town in North Sikkim, serving as a junction for routes to Lachen and Lachung.

Qutab Minar.description: A historic minaret located in Delhi, India, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

veranda.description: A roofed, open-air gallery or porch attached to the outside of a building, common in Indian architecture.

dhobi.description: A traditional Indian washerman who washes clothes for a living.

Pritex.description: Mentioned as a probable private detective agency involved in the investigation.

yoga.description: A physical, mental, and spiritual practice originating from ancient India.

telegram.description: A written message sent by telegraph, a common means of communication before the digital age.

Buddha.description: The founder of Buddhism, whose life and teachings are depicted in the monastery.

shamiana.description: A decorative tent or canopy used for outdoor gatherings and ceremonies in India.

paisa.description: A small unit of Indian currency, equal to one-hundredth of a rupee.

Bengal.description: A region in eastern India, home to Feluda and his companions.

Egypt.description: An ancient civilization referenced in comparison to Tibet.

Iraq.description: A country in the Middle East, referenced as the site of ancient civilizations.

Mesopotamia.description: An ancient historical region, referenced as one of the world's earliest civilizations.

India.description: The country where the story is set and whose cultural heritage is discussed.

Charminar.description: A brand of Indian cigarettes offered by Feluda during the séance.

bearer.description: A domestic servant or attendant, often responsible for serving food and drinks.

seances.description: Spiritual gatherings intended to communicate with the dead, often involving rituals or mediums.

Virendra Shelvankar.description: Mr Shelvankar's son and a suspect in the case, identified during a séance as the alleged murderer.

SKM 463.description: A vehicle registration number, referring to a specific jeep involved in the investigation.

trunk call.description: A long-distance telephone call, especially one made within India.

Mall.description: In Indian hill stations, 'Mall' refers to the main promenade or central street where people gather.

Sikkim orange.description: A type of orange grown in Sikkim, here referring to a beverage made from it.

Agfa.description: A well-known German brand of photographic products, such as film and cameras.

Florence.description: A historic city in Italy, mentioned as a place where Helmut worked.

Heidelburg.description: A city in Germany, where Helmut's parents met and married.

Kathmandu.description: The capital of Nepal, referenced as a place where Helmut stayed at a monastery.

Buddha Purnima.description: A major Buddhist festival celebrating the birth, enlightenment, and death of Gautama Buddha.

hippies.description: A term for members of a countercultural movement of the 1960s and 70s, some of whom traveled to India seeking spiritual experiences.

leech.description: A blood-sucking worm found in wet environments, common in the hills of India.

Thondup.description: The jeep driver with a Tibetan name, described as tall and dressed in black.

Singtham.description: A town in Sikkim passed through on the way to Pemiangchi.

Namchi.description: Namchi, sometimes referred to as Namche, is a town in Sikkim known for being dry and clean, where the group stops briefly.

Rangeet.description: Another river in Sikkim, noted for its clear, greenish water.

Baisakh.description: The first month of the Bengali and Indian solar calendar, corresponding to April-May.

England.description: A country in Europe, referenced in relation to birch trees.

galoshes.description: Waterproof overshoes worn to protect regular shoes from rain or mud.

sadhubaba.description: A holy man or ascetic in India, often smeared with ash as a sign of renunciation.

chowkidar.description: A watchman or caretaker, typically employed to look after property or buildings.

Ghatshila.description: A town in eastern India, mentioned as the supposed location of Mr Bose's nephew's wedding.

Chaitra.description: The last month of the Bengali calendar, traditionally considered inauspicious for Hindu weddings.

bungalow.description: A type of single-storied house, common in India, especially as colonial-era residences.

tobacoo.description: Tobacco (sometimes misspelled as 'tobacoo') is a substance smoked or chewed, here used with salt to remove leeches.
